summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with a one-day history of chills, fatigue, nausea, and watery diarrhea. Given his history of HCV cirrhosis, portopulmonary hypertension, and active liver transplant status, he was evaluated for possible infection. Workup included negative blood, urine, stool, and ascitic fluid cultures, with no evidence of bacterial infection or spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. A therapeutic paracentesis removed 3 liters of fluid, and imaging showed mild pulmonary edema likely due to decompensation from the viral illness. Empiric antibiotics were discontinued after 48 hours due to negative cultures, and diarrhea resolved with supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue home medications, use loperamide as needed, run tube feeds continuously, and monitor weight. Follow-up was arranged with his PCP and liver clinic.
